findings.explanation: The module grants each sink's unique writer identity write access on storage, pubsub and bigquery destinations, but a sink with destination_type logging and an explicit destination in another project gets nothing. Cloud Logging needs roles/logging.bucketWriter on the destination project for cross-project log bucket routing (same-project buckets need no grant and have no writer identity), so those sinks apply cleanly and then drop every entry. No rule can see the asymmetry between the grant resources and the sink map.
findings.remediation: Grant roles/logging.bucketWriter (conditioned on the destination bucket's resource name) to the writer identity of each cross-project logging sink. The grant's for_each must be filtered on the destination's project, which is unknown at plan when destination is a computed value, so a plan-safe module-side grant needs an explicit opt-in input; until then the variable description documents the manual grant.
findings.title: Sinks routed to a log bucket in another project get no roles/logging.bucketWriter grant, so their logs are silently not delivered

findings.explanation: var.kms_key_name is only checked for being non-empty and var.location only for not being global, yet Cloud Logging requires the CMEK key to live in the bucket's location. A mismatch (or a key name that is not a full crypto key ID) plans cleanly, grants the service agent on the key, then fails creating the bucket. Best-fit principle: apply-time correctness.
findings.remediation: Validate kms_key_name as a full crypto key ID and add a lifecycle precondition on the bucket that the key's /locations/<location>/ segment matches var.location.
findings.title: CMEK key location is never checked against the log bucket location, so a mismatch fails only at apply with an API error

findings.explanation: HLD_GCP_105 could not follow the sink's destination through the module boundary; resolved, the sink targets google_storage_bucket.logs, whose retention_policy has no is_locked, so archived log objects can still be shortened or removed by anyone who can edit the bucket. This is the example only; the module cannot see the destination bucket.
findings.remediation: Set retention_policy.is_locked = true on the archive bucket, or suppress HLD_GCP_105/HLD_GCP_147 on the example with a reason. Locking is irreversible and blocks deleting the example's objects for 30 days, so it is a judgment call for a demo configuration.
findings.suppression_reason: Demo configuration: locking a GCS retention policy is irreversible and would block teardown of the example for 30 days
findings.title: Example's errors-to-storage sink archives to a bucket whose retention policy is not locked

findings.explanation: The example's audit-to-log-bucket sink routes every cloudaudit.googleapis.com entry into the module's central log bucket, but the module call leaves locked at its default of false. Anyone holding logging.buckets.update can cut retention_days to the minimum or delete the bucket, discarding the audit trail the bucket exists to keep. No built-in policy checks locked on google_logging_project_bucket_config (only HLD_GCP_129 retention and HLD_GCP_349 CMEK), and the sink-to-bucket link crosses the module boundary. It is the log-bucket counterpart of HOLDEN_AI_003.
findings.remediation: Pass locked = true in the module call for buckets that hold audit logs. Locking is irreversible (the bucket cannot be deleted until every entry ages out of its 400-day retention), so for a demo configuration either lock it deliberately or record why it stays unlocked.
findings.suppression_reason: Demo configuration: locking is irreversible and the log bucket could not be deleted until its 400-day retention expired
findings.title: Example routes all audit logs into the central log bucket without locking its retention

findings.explanation: The bucket's depends_on only orders creation after google_kms_crypto_key_iam_member.logging_service_agent returns; Cloud KMS IAM grants take up to a few minutes to propagate, and Cloud Logging checks the service agent's access to the key when it creates a CMEK bucket. On a fresh project the first apply can fail with a permission error on the key and succeed on re-run. Best-fit principle: apply-time correctness.
findings.remediation: Insert a time_sleep (hashicorp/time, create_duration around 60s) triggered by the key grant and make the bucket depend on it, or document that a first apply may need a re-run. Adding the time provider is a module interface change, so weigh it against documenting the retry.
findings.title: CMEK log bucket is created straight after its KMS grant, so IAM propagation lag can fail the first apply

suggested_policies.rationale: HLD_GCP_105 requires a locked retention policy when a sink writes to a GCS bucket, but nothing covers the equivalent for sinks that write to a Cloud Logging bucket: google_logging_project_bucket_config has no check on locked. An unlocked log bucket lets anyone with logging.buckets.update shorten retention or delete the bucket, so routed logs can be purged early. The check is one sink attribute plus one referenced-resource attribute, the same shape as HLD_GCP_105.
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: LOCAL_GCP_001
name: Cloud Logging sinks to a log bucket must target a bucket with a locked retention policy
principle: data-protection
severity: MEDIUM
rationale: |
  A sink that routes to a Cloud Logging bucket whose retention is not locked
  lets anyone with logging.buckets.update shorten retention_days or delete the
  bucket, purging the routed logs before their retention period ends. Locking
  makes the retention immutable, the log-bucket equivalent of GCS Bucket Lock.
message: |
  google_logging_project_sink routes to a google_logging_project_bucket_config
  that does not set locked = true.
remediation: |
  Lock the destination bucket's retention (irreversible):

    resource "google_logging_project_bucket_config" "audit" {
      retention_days = 365
      locked         = true
    }
resources:
  google_logging_project_sink:
    filter:
      path: destination
      matches: '^logging\.googleapis\.com/'
    references:
      type: google_logging_project_bucket_config
      via: destination
      must:
        path: locked
        equals: true
        required: true
